'''Dominic Gaudreault Dom Goes To Florida (tournament report)''' is the tournament report [[Dominic Gaudreault]] posted on DeckTech on 12 October 2000 about [[2000 Decipher World Championship]].<ref name="tr-d1333">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-12-dom-goes-to-floridad1333/ dom-goes-to-florida], DeckTech (Dominic "Decktech" Gaudreault, 12 October 2000). Preservation copy: [https://stevetotheizz0.github.io/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-12-dom-goes-to-floridad1333/ GitHub Pages].</ref> Dominic Gaudreault finished 4th on Day 1 (6–2), took the last Day 3 seat on Day 2 (5–3, one differential ahead of Martin Akesson), and finished 5th after going 2–2 on Day 3, 13–7 in all.

== Report info ==
* '''Author:''' [[Dominic Gaudreault]] (byline: Dominic "Decktech" Gaudreault)
* '''Published:''' 12 October 2000 (DeckTech)
* '''Report title:''' ''Dom Goes To Florida''
* '''Event:''' [[2000 Decipher World Championship]]
* '''Event date:''' October 2000
* '''Site:''' Florida
* '''Finish:''' 5th
* '''Record:''' 13–7
* '''Dark deck:''' [[2000 Decipher World Championship Dominic Gaudreault Why I Finish 5 at World|"The Machine" Bring Him Before Me (26–0 before Worlds), all three days]]
* '''Light deck:''' [[2000 Decipher World Championship Dominic Gaudreault Dominic World 1-2 PILE|Echo Base Operations with Baragwin, Off the Edge and the Super Falcon, Days 1–2 (Honor of the Jedi and Uncontrollable Fury added for Day 2)]]
* '''Light deck:''' Copy of an old Yannick Lapointe deck with about seven cards changed, Day 3

== Other results named in the report ==

* about 37th (Day 1): [[Raphael Asselin]]
* 13th (Day 2), one differential behind Gaudreault: [[Martin Akesson]]
* Dropped on Day 2 ('3-4 drop'): [[Alex Klammrodt]]
* 2nd: [[Yannick Lapointe]]
* 1st: [[Matt Sokol]]

== Discrepancies ==

Where this report disagrees with other sources, the wiki keeps the other record and notes the difference here.

* Gaudreault writes that Alex Klammrodt 'did 3-4 drop' on Day 2, but the Decipher Day 2 log on the hub gives Klammrodt 4 (−10) with 2 of 8 games missed, i.e. 2–4. (see [[2000 Decipher World Championship]])
